scenarioSubtitle: Designing an AI-enabled SME customer journey
description: Participants make AI leadership decisions across the customer journey and see how those choices affect customer economic value over time.

rounds.title: How should we use AI in SME acquisition emails?
rounds.prompt: The bank wants to use AI to improve how it reaches and attracts SME customers. Should AI personalise every marketing message, focus only on high-value prospects, or be left out entirely?

options.label: Use AI to personalise every email for every SME customer
options.explanation: Every email becomes more relevant, but acquisition is not where AI adds the most value. The cost of running AI on every contact reduces efficiency and creates a small drag on later stages.

options.label: Use AI to personalise only the most important messages and high-value prospects
options.explanation: This balances relevance with cost. The right customers get a personalised experience, and the benefit carries through into onboarding, activation, and beyond.

options.label: Use standard campaign software with no AI personalisation
options.explanation: Without personalisation, fewer prospects engage. This reduces conversion rates and limits value across every stage of the journey.

rounds.title: How should the AI support onboarding?
rounds.prompt: The bank is setting up how AI will support new SME customers during onboarding. Should AI handle the whole process automatically, guide customers step by step, or stay out of it entirely?

options.label: Automate the full onboarding process — fast, but with no explanation or human backup
options.explanation: Onboarding is fast, but customers are left without clear explanations at a critical moment. Initial efficiency quickly turns into lost confidence — hurting activation, engagement, and retention throughout the journey.

options.label: Guide customers through onboarding with AI, explain each step clearly, and offer human help when needed
options.explanation: This makes onboarding smooth without leaving customers confused. Clear guidance and easy access to human support build confidence — and that confidence carries through every stage, all the way to loyalty.

options.label: Keep the existing manual onboarding process with standard digital forms
options.explanation: Avoiding AI avoids short-term risk, but leaves a slow and fragmented experience in place. The impact shows immediately at onboarding and compounds through every stage that follows.

rounds.title: How proactive should the AI be in helping the customer get started?
rounds.prompt: The SME customer has just onboarded and needs to start using the service. Should AI actively guide them, respond to their behaviour, or leave them to find their own way?

options.label: Immediately push AI-driven prompts and recommendations to all new customers
options.explanation: More customers take action early, but the constant prompts feel pushy. Trust starts to erode and the initial gain reverses through engagement and retention.

options.label: Use AI to suggest helpful next steps based on what the customer has done and what they are likely to need
options.explanation: Customers get timely, relevant guidance without feeling overwhelmed. The result is strong activation that builds naturally into deeper engagement and loyalty.

options.label: Leave customers to explore the product on their own, with no AI guidance
options.explanation: Without guidance, many customers struggle to get started. Activation stalls and the experience never fully builds momentum through engagement.

rounds.title: How much autonomy should the AI have in ongoing support?
rounds.prompt: The bank is deciding how its AI will behave day-to-day. Should the AI act on its own, work alongside the customer with clear controls, or only respond when asked?

options.label: Allow AI to act independently across most interactions and decisions, without asking for customer input
options.explanation: Customers benefit in the short term, but acting without asking creates unease. Trust erodes significantly — and the damage at retention and loyalty is among the sharpest in the entire simulation.

options.label: Use AI to proactively help customers, but always show what it is doing and give them control over important actions
options.explanation: This is the most effective approach: AI is helpful and proactive, but customers stay in control. The improvement at engagement is the largest in this stage — and it flows strongly through expansion, retention, and loyalty.

options.label: Keep AI in the background — only showing information when the customer asks for it
options.explanation: AI is underused at the stage where it would add the most value. The experience feels static and limited — and engagement, expansion, and retention all take a compounding hit.

rounds.title: How should AI shape growth offers and recommendations?
rounds.prompt: The SME is now an active customer. The bank wants to use AI to identify growth opportunities and offer relevant products. How should it approach this?

options.label: Use AI to send the same growth offers to all customers, without personalising by business context
options.explanation: More customers receive offers, which boosts short-term expansion. But generic offers feel irrelevant to many customers — and that erodes loyalty at the end of the journey.

options.label: Use AI to match growth offers to each customer's actual situation — based on their behaviour, business signals, and likely needs
options.explanation: AI acts as a genuine growth partner — identifying the right offer at the right time for each customer. This produces the largest single-stage value lift in the simulation, and it holds through retention and loyalty.

options.label: Make no proactive offers — wait for customers to ask about new products themselves
options.explanation: Without proactive offers, the bank misses customers at exactly the moment they are ready to grow. The lost opportunity compounds into lower retention and loyalty.

rounds.title: How should the AI respond to emerging risk and churn signals?
rounds.prompt: The bank's systems are picking up early signs that some customers may be struggling or thinking of leaving. How should AI use these signals to respond?

options.label: Allow AI to act automatically when it detects a risk — without explaining to the customer what it is doing or why
options.explanation: Some customers are retained, but acting without explanation at a sensitive moment seriously damages trust. The short-term retention gain fully reverses into loyalty loss — a clear consequence of acting without transparency.

options.label: Use AI to spot risk early and offer the customer clear, practical support — explaining what has been detected and what options are available
options.explanation: This is the highest-impact decision in the simulation. AI detects risk early, offers relevant support, and keeps the customer informed throughout. The effect on retention and loyalty is the most powerful in the entire journey.

options.label: Take no action until the customer contacts the bank or clearly shows signs of leaving
options.explanation: Waiting means the bank only responds after significant damage has already been done. The loss in retention and loyalty is immediate and clearly visible on the chart.
